analysis.title: US Daily: Adding a Third Hike in March
key_insights: October core CPI rose 30bp, a third straight month of worse inflation news. GS estimates residual seasonality tied to last year's government shutdown added 5bp, but the upside surprises spanned several categories and went beyond direct oil pass-through.
GS adds a third 25bp hike in March 2027 to its forecast, taking the funds rate to a peak of 4.25-4.5%. It still expects a second 25bp hike in December.

A third hike could come in January instead. GS thinks March is a bit more likely because it expects softer November and December inflation, with core PCE in the high teens, followed by larger start-of-year price increases (the 'January effect') that lift January inflation.
GS estimates October CPI implies a 35bp increase in core PCE prices. November price data will not be released until after the December 9 FOMC meeting.

Governor Waller said before the CPI release that a 50bp hike should be considered in December if October core CPI was around 0.3 percent or higher, and that a 25bp hike would put credibility at risk. GS still expects 25bp because it thinks most FOMC voters would hesitate to jump to 50bp.

GS expects most FOMC participants to signal a third hike in the December dot plot. This would take only two additional participants raising their forecasts. Firmer January inflation would make delivering the hike the path of least resistance even if the energy shock appears over.

Oil futures have fallen substantially since the elections. GS says that if prices follow the futures or its commodity strategists' similar forecast, the bulk of the energy-shock pass-through to consumer prices should already be behind us.
GS remains confident inflation will be meaningfully lower by the end of 2027 as the effects of tariffs, the energy shock and AI price pressures fade.
Terminal fed funds rate forecast is unchanged at 3.25-3.5%, but rate cuts now begin in December 2027 (previously September 2027), followed by cuts in March, June and September 2028.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Upside surprise and a third month of worse inflation news. GS estimates 5bp of the figure comes from residual shutdown-related seasonality.
GS estimate implied by the October CPI data, ahead of the PCE release.
GS expects softer readings before larger start-of-year increases lift January inflation.
Peak after three 25bp hikes: December 2026, plus March 2027 added to the earlier forecast.
Unchanged. The cutting cycle starts one quarter later than previously forecast.
GS baseline, against Waller's suggestion that 50bp should be considered.
Pushed back from September 2027, with further cuts in March, June and September 2028.

risk_factors: Firmer-than-expected January inflation from start-of-year price increases could pull the third hike forward or make it the path of least resistance.
FOMC could move faster than every other meeting. A 50bp December hike is possible per Waller.
Ongoing elevated cost pressures from tariffs, the energy shock and AI price pressures.
Residual seasonality tied to last year's government shutdown can distort inflation prints.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish read: recent inflation prints lead most FOMC participants to signal a third hike in the December dot plot, and Waller floats a 50bp December hike. Firmer January inflation would make a hike the path of least resistance.
tension_points.bear_case: Oil futures have fallen substantially since the elections, so the bulk of energy pass-through should be behind us. GS expects softer November and December inflation and meaningfully lower inflation by end-2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Softer-than-expected January inflation, since GS says the March hike depends on larger start-of-year price increases boosting January inflation.

theme_stances.key_argument: Recent inflation prints will lead most FOMC participants to signal a third hike, and firmer January inflation would make delivering it the path of least resistance.
theme_stances.evidence: we are adding a third 25bp hike to our forecast in March 2027
